passage: I'm Kavitha, and the first time I felt my own voice work for me was at a scholarship interview. My hands were cold, my heart was thudding, and Ayesha, my friend, had told me before I went in, "Feel your feet, breathe from your belly, speak like you're telling a friend." So I sat tall, breathed out slowly and started. My voice came out lower and steadier than I expected. The panel leaned in. I still felt nervous inside. It was steady on the outside, though, which surprised me. Later Ayesha said I sounded composed, and I said I wasn't at all. So a steady voice doesn't always mean a calm mind, I think, but it helped me.

qa.q: What did Ayesha tell Kavitha before the interview?
qa.a: Ayesha told Kavitha to feel the feet on the floor, breathe from the belly and speak as if telling a friend.

qa.q: What was Kavitha feeling under that steady voice?
qa.a: Kavitha was nervous, with cold hands and a thudding heart, even though Kavitha's voice sounded composed. The steady sound came from breath and posture, not from a calm mind.

qa.q: What could Kavitha do before the next interview?
qa.a: Sit tall, breathe out slowly and feel the feet on the floor, as Kavitha did, and practise speaking as if telling a friend.

qa.q: How did Ayesha see Kavitha's voice?
qa.a: Ayesha heard it as composed and did not know how nervous Kavitha felt inside.

grounding: A young adult speaks with a resonant steady voice in an interview, which can signal composure even when nervous, and breath and posture help.

passage: Note from Ms. Gopika, faculty mentor. On Friday I sat on the panel for the final-year project presentations. Arnab walked to the front, stood with his feet apart and took a long breath before starting. His voice was deep, even and clear across the hall, and he made eye contact with each examiner in turn. The room settled. I noticed his hand around the clicker was white at the knuckles, and afterwards he told me he'd been dreading it all week. So the steady voice was partly practice and partly effort. I told him what I saw and suggested he keep the breathing, and Arnab said he would do exactly that in the next viva.

qa.q: Where did Arnab stand while starting?
qa.a: Arnab stood at the front with his feet apart.

qa.q: What did the white knuckles suggest about Arnab's feelings?
qa.a: They suggested Arnab was nervous under the steady voice, which he confirmed by saying he had dreaded the presentation. The voice showed composure, but not the whole picture.

qa.q: What could Arnab keep doing in the next viva?
qa.a: Keep the long breath and steady stance before speaking, since they helped his voice come out even and clear.

qa.q: How might the examiners have seen Arnab's voice?
qa.a: They probably took it as composed and confident, as the room settled, without seeing the tight grip on the clicker.

grounding: A young adult presents with a resonant steady voice that signals composure, though nervous people can sound steady too.
